sec: Peg, cirrhogenic dose, alcoholic hepatitis mortality/marker, progression diagram, alcohol metabolism

items.q: How is '1 peg' defined at the top of the chapter?
Cirrhogenic dose — match — 1) Male 2) Female … A) 20–40 gm/day (1 peg) B) 40–80 g/day (2 pegs)
items.exp: Male: 40–80 g/day (2 pegs); Female: 20–40 gm/day (1 peg). (Book p1026)

items.q: The cirrhogenic dose must be consumed for how long to produce cirrhosis?
items.exp: '→ 5 days a week for 15 years → Cirrhosis.' (Book p1026)

items.q: Alcoholic hepatitis: printed mortality and best serum marker?
items.exp: 'Mortality 70%' and 'Best Serum marker : Carbohydrate deficient transferrin'. (Book p1026)

items.q: In the progression diagram, alcohol consumption leads to alcoholic fatty liver after how long, and is that stage reversible?
items.exp: 'Alcohol Consumption —3–5 years→ Alcoholic fatty liver (Reversible)'. (Book p1026)

items.q: From the fatty-liver branch point, judge: I Cirrhosis begins micronodular and progresses to macronodular. II In macronodular cirrhosis the nucleus is pushed to the periphery. III Cirrhosis carries risk of HCC.
opts: I and III true, II false
I true, II and III false
II and III true, I false
items.exp: Cirrhosis → micronodular → Progress → macronodular (Nucleus pushed to periphery); → Risk of HCC. (Book p1026)

items.q: The other branch from alcoholic fatty liver is alcoholic hepatitis (high mortality). What cause is printed beneath it?
items.exp: 'Alcoholic hepatitis (High mortality) — Cause : Binge drinking'. (Book p1026)

items.q: Alcohol metabolism — which of the following is NOT one of the three enzymes branched in the diagram?
items.exp: Enzyme: Aldehyde dehydrogenase; Cyt P2E1; Catalase. (Book p1026)

items.q: Fill up the pathway: Alcohol → ______ (toxic to liver) —aldehyde dehydrogenase→ metabolic products.
items.exp: 'Alcohol → Acetaldehyde —Aldehyde dehydrogenase→ metabolic products'; 'Acetaldehyde → Toxic to liver'. (Book p1026)

items.q: Two men drink identically; one carries an aldehyde-dehydrogenase polymorphism making him a poor metaboliser. Per the diagram, what is his particular risk?
opts: Protected, because less acetaldehyde is formed
Higher carbohydrate-deficient transferrin but no liver risk
items.exp: Polymorphism → Efficient metaboliser / Poor metaboliser: 'Prone to develop alcohol hepatitis'. (Book p1026)
